obernants.operator: Universe U is candidate implementations x named outcomes. A wrong implementation violating a sampled assertion cannot yield all-pass. The compiled production mutant targeting signed_wide_total_and_ties is a witnessed exclusion. Unsampled defects can still pass; finite coverage is explicit.

obernants.operator: Independent witness: 4096 signed/absent graphs on four vertices compare independent subset enumeration and transitive closure, plus exact signed extremes, parallel ties, loops, isolates, invalid endpoints and both caps. The oracle uses a distinct representation or exhaustive candidate enumeration; self-roundtrip alone is insufficient.

obernants.operator: In exhaustive_small_signed_forests the oracle fixes target transitive closure and considers subsets with exactly n-components edges. Equality of closure plus this edge count forces an acyclic spanning forest; deleting the rank condition would admit extra negative edges on cycles and solve a different optimization. Each of six potential edges is independently absent or weighted -1,0,1, giving 4096 assignments. A triangle of three -1 edges distinguishes unconstrained connected-subgraph weight -3 from forest optimum -2.

obernants.operator: signed_wide_total_and_ties fixes two selected i64::MIN edges and asserts total=2*i128::from(i64::MIN), outside i64 range, plus exact selected indices and isolates. The compiled production subtraction mutant returns the opposite signed sum and fails this named assertion after successful compilation. The positive i64::MAX path also requires a sum above i64::MAX. These witnesses reject sign reversal and narrow accumulation but do not prove every arithmetic implementation correct.
